brief: ING previews two Friday releases. James Knightley writes financial markets now price an October Fed rate hike as more likely than not, with the September jobs report and the September inflation print (due 14 October) the two data points that determine the decision. August's jobs report beat expectations after a weak run. Given the low-hire, low-fire dynamic still in place, ING expects a downward revision to that August figure and September payrolls near 100k, with unemployment holding at 4.1%. That outcome would keep an October hike in play. Bert Colijn writes eurozone inflation is currently driven mainly by energy prices. Core inflation remains at 2.4%, unchanged from February and from before the Middle East war began, with attention on whether second-round effects are now emerging.
